definitions.explanation: Food, flowers, or other items placed before a deity, Buddha, or the spirits of the deceased as a religious or commemorative offering.

examples.japanese: ⟦{仏壇|ぶつだん}→仏壇：07116_butsudan⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{供|そな}え{物|もの}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{置|お}いた→置く：01092_oku⟧。
examples.english: I placed an offering on the Buddhist altar.

examples.japanese: {供|そな}え{物|もの}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{果物|くだもの}→果物：00509_kudamono⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{下|さ}げて→下げる：00807_sageru⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{食|た}べた→食べる：00396_taberu⟧。
examples.english: I took down the fruit offering and then ate it.

examples.japanese: ⟦お{盆|ぼん}→お盆：05587_obon⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{先祖|せんぞ}→先祖：04040_senzo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{霊|れい}→霊：14667_rei⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ため→ため：01145_tame⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{供|そな}え{物|もの}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{用意|ようい}する→用意する：22428_youisuru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{習慣|しゅうかん}→習慣：01429_shuukan⟧だ。
examples.english: It is a Japanese custom to prepare offerings for the spirits of one's ancestors during Obon.

notes:
USAGE:
Typical offerings include fruit, rice, sweets, flowers, and incense. After being offered, food items are often taken down and eaten by the family — this is called {供|そな}え{物|もの}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{下|さ}げる→下げる：00807_sageru⟧. The word is used for both Buddhist altars (⟦{仏壇|ぶつだん}→仏壇：07116_butsudan⟧) and Shinto shrines (⟦{神棚|かみだな}→神棚：13740_kamidana⟧).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {供|そな}え{物|もの}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{供|そな}える→供える：11562_sonaeru⟧ (to make an offering)
- {供|そな}え{物|もの}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{下|さ}げる→下げる：00807_sageru⟧ (to take down an offering)
- ⟦{神|かみ}→神：02147_kami⟧⟦へ→へ：02473_he⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{供|そな}え{物|もの} (an offering to the gods)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦お{供|そな}え→お供え：25860_osonae⟧: the same word with the polite prefix お, commonly used in everyday speech
- ⟦{奉納|ほうのう}→奉納：12200_hounou⟧: dedication — more formal, refers to dedicating items to a shrine or temple
